This Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is filed by the appellant, challenging the order dated 06.02.2018 passed in M.C.O.P.No.355 of 2017 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal / I Additional District and Sessions Court, Tirunelveli.

sentences.text: respondent herein filed a claim petition, stating that when the deceased person along with pillion rider was waiting at a road junction to cross the road, the bus belonging to the appellant Transport Corporation came in a rash and negligent manner from south to north, lost control and dashed against the motorcycle, which resulted in the accident.

3.The appellant opposed the claim petition, stating that the accident took place only due to the negligence of the deceased and that in any case, the compensation claimed by the respondent was State Express Transport Corporation ... vs Poovarammal on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12325247/
1 excessive.
4.The respondent had examined herself as P.W.1 and an eye witness as P.W.2, besides marking Ex.P.1.

entities.text: State Express Transport Corporation ... vs Poovarammal
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The appellant examined the driver of the bus as R.W.1.
Ex.C.1 to C.6 were marked as Court documents.

5.The Tribunal, after taking into consideration oral and documentary evidence, held that the accident took place only due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the bus belonging to the appellant and determined compensation payable at Rs.11,25,000/- (Rupees Eleven Lakhs and Twenty Five Thousand Only) by the appellant Corporation to the respondent.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 6.The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the manner of the accident would show that the deceased also contributed to the accident and the Tribunal ought to have fixed contributing negligence on the deceased and that in any case, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal was excessive, inasmuch as instead of deducting 50% towards personal expenses, the Tribunal deducted only 1/3rd of the income towards personal expenses, which is erroneous and prayed for a reduction of the compensation.
7.Though notice was sent to the sole respondent and the name is printed in the cause list, none has entered appearance.
8.This Court has considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the appellant and perused the materials available on record.

9.The points involved in the instant appeal are as follows:-
(a) Whether the Tribunal was right in fixing the entire liability on the appellant Corporation?; and (b) Whether the quantum of compensation is just and reasonable?
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 10.As regards the first point, it is seen that the claimant had examined P.W.2 eye witness to show that the deceased was waiting at the junction to cross the road, at which time, the driver of the bus belonging to the appellant lost control and dashed against the deceased.
Per contra, the driver of the bus was examined as R.W.1 to show that the deceased suddenly crossed the road, which resulted in the accident.
A perusal of the rough sketch Ex.C.6 marked as Court document shows that the accident took place on the side of the road, which corroborates the evidence of P.W.2.
Therefore, the evidence of R.W.1, who is an interested witness, cannot be accepted.
Hence, the finding of the Tribunal that the accident took place only due to the rash and negligent driving of the bus belonging to the appellant is justified and in accordance with the law.
Therefore, the first point is answered.

sentences.text: However, no document was marked to prove the income of the deceased.
In such circumstances, the notional income fixed by the Tribunal at Rs.7,500/- is in accordance with law and 25% has to be added towards future prospects.
However, the Tribunal had deducted 1/3rd towards personal e x p e n s e s , t h o u g h t h e d e c e a s e d w a s a b a c h e l o r .
T h e T r i b u n a l o u g h t t o https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis have deducted 50% towards personal expenses.
Hence, the monthly income, after adding 25% towards future prospects, comes to Rs.9,375/-.

Therefore, the amount under the head of loss of income is calculated as follows:-
Rs.9,375 x 12 x 15 x 50/100 = Rs.8,43,750/-.
12.Further
, the respondent is also entitled to a loss of consortium at Rs.40,000/- and the same is now awarded.
The award under the head of loss of estate and funeral expenses is confirmed.

Thus,
the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is modified as follows:-
Heads
Amount
awarded

Amount Award by the Tribunal awarded by this confirmed or Court enhanced or granted or reduced Loss of Income Rs.11,25,000/- Rs.8,43,750/- Reduced Loss of Consortium - Rs.40,000/- Granted Funeral Expenses Rs.15,000/- Rs.15,000/- Confirmed Loss of Estate Rs.15,000/- Rs.15,000/- Confirmed Total Compensation Rs.11,55,000/- Rs.9,13,750/- By reducing a sum of Rs.
2,41,250/-
13.The

appellant Transport Corporation is directed to deposit the award amount modified by this Court together with interest at the rate of 7.5% https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis per annum from the date of the claim petition till the date of realization (excluding the period of dismissal for default if any) and costs, less the amount already deposited, if any, within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
14.On such a deposit, the respondent is permitted to withdraw the same, less the amount, if any,
already withdrawn, by filing an appropriate application before the Tribunal.
15.In the result, this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is partly allowed.
No costs.
Consequently, the connected miscellaneous petition is also closed.
